name: grist
description: Self-hosted relational spreadsheet and lightweight database platform

fields.name: WEB_PORT
fields.label: R1: Web Interface Port
fields.help: Host port used to open Grist in bridge mode. In Host Mode, Grist listens directly on NAS port 8484.

fields.name: GRIST_SESSION_SECRET
fields.label: R2: Session Secret
fields.help: Generated secret used to protect Grist browser sessions. Keep this value stable and private; changing it invalidates existing sessions.

fields.name: GRIST_BOOT_KEY
fields.label: R3: First-Run Boot Key
fields.help:
Generated key proving that you control this Grist installation.
On first access, Grist opens its boot login page. Paste this value there, or open http://NAS-IP:8484/boot. Save it securely because it can also provide emergency access to the Admin Panel later.

fields.name: GRIST_DEFAULT_EMAIL
fields.label: R4: Administrator Email
fields.help:
Email address assigned ownership of the installation and initial organization. Replace the example with the email you will use for authentication.
This is not a username/password login by itself. After entering the boot key, configure an authentication method in Grist's Quick Setup wizard. Changing this email later can transfer administrative ownership and affect access to the single organization.

fields.name: GRIST_SINGLE_ORG
fields.label: R5: Organization Name
fields.help: Name of the single Grist organization created for this installation. Use only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, such as my-company. Avoid changing it after users and documents have been created.

fields.name: DATA_LOCATION
fields.label: R6: Data Folder
fields.help: Host folder for Grist documents, the home database, sessions, configuration, and other persistent application data. Back up this folder regularly.

fields.name: GRIST_NETWORK_MODE
fields.label: O1: Network
fields.help: Choose Create New Bridge for the recommended default, Host Mode, or an existing named Docker network. Bridge mode is normally sufficient for direct access and reverse proxies.

fields.name: APP_HOME_URL
fields.label: O2: Public Application URL
fields.help:
Set this only when Grist is accessed through a domain or reverse proxy. Enter the complete public URL, such as https://grist.example.com, without a trailing slash.
Leave blank for direct NAS-IP access. Grist uses this URL for authentication callbacks, sharing links, and notifications.

fields.name: GRIST_FORCE_LOGIN
fields.label: O3: Require Login
fields.help: Blocks anonymous access when enabled. You must select and configure an authentication method during Grist's first-run Quick Setup wizard, especially before exposing Grist beyond a trusted private network.

fields.name: GRIST_SANDBOX_FLAVOR
fields.label: O4: Formula Sandbox
fields.help:
gVisor isolates Python formulas from other documents, the container, and the network. It is strongly recommended whenever documents may contain formulas from other users.
Some older processors or restricted NAS environments may not support it. Unsandboxed formulas can access anything available to the Grist process and should only be used temporarily for diagnosis.

fields.name: COOKIE_MAX_AGE
fields.label: O5: Login Session Duration
fields.help: Maximum session-cookie age in milliseconds. The default is seven days. Enter none to use a browser-session cookie that should expire when the browser closes.

fields.name: GRIST_TELEMETRY_LEVEL
fields.label: O6: Telemetry
fields.help: Controls Grist usage telemetry. This recipe disables telemetry by default.

fields.name: GRIST_ALLOW_AUTOMATIC_VERSION_CHECKING
fields.label: O7: Automatic Version Checks
fields.help:
Checks weekly for newer Grist versions. For the OSS image this is normally disabled unless explicitly enabled.
When enabled, the check sends Grist Labs the installed version, edition, and an anonymized installation identifier. It does not update the container automatically.

fields.name: GRIST_WIDGET_LIST_URL
fields.label: O8: Widget Gallery Manifest
fields.help: Manifest used to display the official Grist custom-widget gallery. Replace it with your own compatible manifest URL if required.

fields.name: RESTART_POLICY
fields.label: O9: Restart Policy
fields.help: Controls whether the container restarts automatically.

fields.name: GRIST_IMAGE
fields.label: A1: Image
fields.help: Official image containing only Grist's free and open-source Community edition. Change this only if you need a pinned tag or another Grist edition.

fields.name: GRIST_SYS_PTRACE_CAPABILITY
fields.label: A2: SYS_PTRACE for gVisor
fields.help:
Most regular Docker installations can run Grist's gVisor sandbox without this extra capability. If Grist reports that PTRACE is unavailable, enable SYS_PTRACE here and redeploy.
This capability increases container privileges, so leave it disabled unless sandbox diagnostics show it is required.

fields.name: GRIST_PORT_MAPPING
fields.label: A3: Bridge Port Mapping
fields.help: Automatically generated for bridge or an existing Docker network and removed in Host Mode.

fields.name: GRIST_CONTAINER_NAME
fields.label: Container Name
fields.help: EasyDocker sets the container name from the project name.

fields.name: GRIST_INTERNAL_PORT
fields.label: Internal Web Port
fields.help: Recipe-managed Grist port inside the container.

fields.name: GRIST_PERSIST_TARGET
fields.label: Persistent Path Inside Container
fields.help: Recipe-managed internal path for all persistent Grist data.

ui.overview: Grist combines spreadsheet editing with relational data, Python formulas, forms, APIs, and collaborative workspaces.
what_happens: One Grist Community edition container will be created using the free and open-source image
Documents, databases, sessions, and installation settings will be stored in the bind-mounted data folder
EasyDocker will generate both the session secret and first-run boot key
On first access, paste the displayed boot key into Grist's boot login page and complete the Quick Setup wizard
The administrator email identifies the installation owner but does not create a password; configure an authentication method during Quick Setup
Anonymous access is disabled by default, but authentication must still be configured before exposing Grist publicly
Python formulas will use the recommended gVisor sandbox by default; SYS_PTRACE can be enabled from Advanced settings if sandbox diagnostics require it
Telemetry is disabled by default while automatic version notifications remain enabled
The official custom-widget gallery is enabled by default
Bridge networking is selected by default, with Host Mode and existing Docker networks also available
ui.data_location: The data folder can be relative to this app's config folder or an absolute host path. It contains documents and databases, so include it in regular backups before upgrades or migrations.
